messages:
anya: Heads-up from field: several customers reported bursty retries after device sleep -> huge spikes in our hosted API quota usage. Repro'd on Android emulator. Thoughts? :grimacing:

sam: Probably backoff scheduling using System.currentTimeMillis. On Android you must use SystemClock.elapsedRealtime to avoid wall-clock jumps.

anya: SDK stores nextRetryAt in SharedPreferences as epoch millis. Quick fix was to store remaining delay instead. Example I pushed to my branch: 
```
// save remaining
prefs.edit().putLong("retry_remaining_ms", backoffMs).apply()
// on restore
val remaining = prefs.getLong("retry_remaining_ms", 0L)
handler.postDelayed(task, remaining.coerceAtLeast(0L))
```

leo: Also add jitter. We accidentally seeded Random with System.currentTimeMillis()%100 leading to identical jitter across processes after reboot. Use ThreadLocalRandom.current().nextLong(0, jitterMs).

sam: And if you persist absolute deadlines, compute remaining using monotonic clock: savedDeadline - SystemClock.elapsedRealtime(). Don't persist wall times.

docs-bot: docs/update: added note "Use monotonic deadlines for backoff scheduling" to SDK best-practices (PR #412).

anya: I'll roll patch and add an emulator e2e that simulates doze and wake. Thanks!
